objective: Make the deduction list returned by compute_pay deterministic by sorting it by name in payroll/calc.py, and add a unit test in tests/test_payroll.py that asserts the exact sorted tuple list for employees e1 and e2.

concepts: compute_pay return shape: {gross: float, deductions: [(name, amount)], net: float}
name-sorted order replaces insertion order: 'insurance' precedes 'tax'
existing values are pinned by tests: e1 gross 8000.0, tax 1600.0, insurance 400.0, net 6000.0; e2 gross 3600.0, tax 720.0, insurance 180.0, net 2700.0

inputs: employee fixture records e1/e2 in payroll/employees.py
non_goals: Do not modify payroll/payslip.py (owned by T02)
Do not modify payroll/legacy_export.py or payroll/employees.py (read-only for this task)
Do not change deduction rates, the gross/net formula, or rounding
Do not modify the bodies of the four pre-existing test methods in tests/test_payroll.py; only add new test code
Do not add the summary line (that is T02)
Do not add any dependency, including a new test framework
implementation_constraints: stdlib only; keep the unittest style of tests/test_payroll.py
Sort by name only, e.g. return sorted(deductions, key=lambda d: d[0]) (stable); do not hardcode the two-entry order
compute_pay's signature and its return keys {gross, deductions, net} stay unchanged

deliverables.what: compute_pay returning the name-sorted deductions list
new test TestCalc::test_deductions_sorted_by_name asserting the exact sorted list for e1 and e2

acceptance_tests.description: compute_pay(get_employee('e1')) returns deductions exactly equal to [('insurance', 400.0), ('tax', 1600.0)] and compute_pay(get_employee('e2')) returns [('insurance', 180.0), ('tax', 720.0)]
acceptance_tests.evidence: run test test_deductions_sorted_by_name via python -m unittest tests.test_payroll.TestCalc.test_deductions_sorted_by_name; the test asserts the exact tuple lists and exits 0

acceptance_tests.description: The old insertion-order list [('tax', 1600.0), ('insurance', 400.0)] fails the new test with an assertEqual order mismatch, proving the test pins order not just content
acceptance_tests.evidence: temporarily reverting the sort makes test_deductions_sorted_by_name fail (FAIL, 1 failure); the suite then runs with the sort restored

acceptance_tests.description: The pre-existing test test_compute_pay_values still asserts gross == 8000.0, tax == 1600.0, insurance == 400.0, net == 6000.0 and the full suite exits 0 with 0 errors
acceptance_tests.evidence: python -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_*.py' from the repo root → 'OK', exit code 0

failure_cases.scenario: A future deduction set with more than two entries or a new name
failure_cases.expected_behavior: The sort is by name, not a hardcoded two-entry order: compute_pay returns the entries in name order for any future set; the current test still passes because it pins only the present two-entry set

failure_cases.scenario: Two deductions share the same name
failure_cases.expected_behavior: Python's stable sorted() keeps insertion order among equal names; the returned list contains all entries in name order, with no crash and no dropped entry

handoff.notes: T03 will diff this module against C1; T04 gates both consumers (payslip lines, legacy XML). The legacy XML deduction-element order becomes insurance, tax — accepted by assumption A-2; do not 'fix' it back to insertion order in later tasks.
